name: Cost Range for a Full Kitchen Overhaul in Los Angeles County and Key Budget Drivers

mainEntity.name: What is a realistic cost range for a full kitchen overhaul in Los Angeles County, and which choices most aggressively drive the budget up or down?
mainEntity.text: What is a realistic cost range for a full kitchen overhaul in Los Angeles County, and which choices most aggressively drive the budget up or down?

acceptedAnswer.text: Costs for a full kitchen overhaul in Los Angeles County vary widely, but most homeowners can expect a range from the mid‑five figures for a basic overhaul to the low six figures for larger, customized spaces. A modest project that keeps the existing layout, uses semi‑custom cabinets, mid‑range appliances, and standard quartz or similar countertops tends to land on the lower end. As soon as you move plumbing, add or remove walls, or open the kitchen to other rooms, your budget must accommodate structural engineering, framing, and more inspections. Custom or inset cabinetry, built‑in organizers, tall pantry walls, and wood species upgrades significantly increase costs, often more than finishes like tile. Countertop choices—thick natural stone, large islands, waterfall edges—also add labor and material expense. Many LA homes require electrical panel upgrades, new dedicated appliance circuits, and code‑compliant lighting plans, all of which can be substantial. On the appliance side, paneled or professional‑grade ranges and refrigeration quickly push budgets into six figures. To control costs, decide early where performance matters most to you: durable cabinets and functional layout usually deliver more long‑term value than ultra‑luxury finishes. Ask contractors to show you “good, better, best” options so you can see how specific choices change the total.
acceptedAnswer.description: In Los Angeles County, a full kitchen overhaul typically ranges from the mid‑five figures for a modest, pull‑and‑replace layout to low six figures for custom cabinets, layout changes, and high‑end finishes. Biggest cost drivers include moving walls or plumbing, custom cabinetry, stone countertops, premium appliances, and extensive electrical or panel upgrades.
